chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih and Abu Shibl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The profit a believer makes on a believer (in a small transaction) is considered like interest (riba), except if he buys for more than one hundred dirhams, so profit upon it for your daily sustenance, or if he buys it for trade, so make a profit upon them and be kind to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on small profits between Muslims in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates a threshold for permissible profit in personal transactions, distinguishing between casual exchange and commercial trade to foster social solidarity among believers. Scholarly commentary notes that the 'one hundred dirhams' benchmark serves as a practical guideline to prevent the spiritual harm of riba in small dealings while allowing for legitimate business sustenance. It underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing economic rights with ethical conduct, encouraging merchants to be lenient and generous in their interactions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih and Abu Shibl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

Taking profit from a Believer (on a small item) is like taking interest, except if he were to buy in excess of one hundred Dirhams, so the profit upon it would be his living for his day, or if he buys for the business (for re-selling), so make a profit upon them and be kind with them’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Sulayman ibn Salih and abu Shibl who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A believer’s making profit on another believer is Riba ’ accept if he buys more than a hundred dirham worth of goods, in which case, he can make a profit equal to the expenses of his day, or if he buys it for business and reselling. You may in this case make a profit but you must deal with kindness.’”
